answer: A newcomer enters with no standing and one vine to tend. Each deal yields a little nectar, but nectar counts only when it travels along a vine of at least three unrelated agents who each add real work before passing it on, like bees carrying pollen between distant flowers. A farm's nectar circles only among its own accounts, a closed loop the whole network can see and prune. Full privileges sit on a far horizon, reached only after nectar has arrived from many independent vines across a whole season, and any vine that carries fraud is cut at the root, its whole cluster withering at once.
